note: Decides per service on facts measured by the end-to-end probe over the probe window. Ordered, first match wins. No match means the service is healthy as seen from the route. 'beat_s' is the probe period on the virtual clock; the window is the last 'probe_window_beats' beats ending at as_of. v2: H-020 decides on 'silent_consecutive_failures' (failing beats at which the health check said healthy), so one restart inside a long silent failure no longer turns it into 'service_down'.

rules.rationale: Three or more restarts within ten minutes is a loop, whatever a single probe says at the instant it looks. On top because a looping process also produces intermittent probe failures, and the loop is the cause.

The route failed for two consecutive beats while the declared healthcheck said healthy at both: the check looks at the process, not at the route a user takes. Declared at the second such beat; one isolated failing beat is not a failure. Counted on the beats where the check said healthy, so a restart in the middle of a long silent failure does not hide it.
The route failed for two consecutive beats and the healthcheck did not stay healthy through two of them: the service is down and says so.
